protocol.cost_impl: single 3N-dim residual block (cross-checked against per-point costs)
protocol.init_random: uniform random rotation (scipy Rotation.random), t ~ U(-1,1)^3

comparison.framing: **Honest framing.** Theseus is a *local* optimiser: each call returns one pose and has no notion of the enumerated mode set or of the z>0 physicality filter that P1 applies. From GT it recovers the nearest minimum (local convergence, not a baseline win). From a cold/random init it recovers whichever basin the descent enters -- on this near-tied cost that is often the P1 flip mode or a non-physical (behind-camera) pose, which the layer's mode enumeration rejects by construction. Theseus also returns no posterior, so it is not comparable to the Laplace mean as an estimator; it is the natural *no-enumeration* reference point. A negative or mixed result is reported as-is: local optimisation does not replace mode enumeration on this cost. Two concrete observations: (i) on 000010/72, the frame where P1's *global* argmin is 44 deg from GT, the GT-init solve lands on the 3.8 deg mode (P1's k1 candidate) -- a local minimum that is closer to GT than the global argmin, so the GT-init row is not simply 'hard argmin'; (ii) the identity-init solve usually ends at a rotation ~70-180 deg from GT, i.e. a non-physical (behind-camera) stationary point of the unconstrained cost.

caveats: The Theseus problem is the *full* (R,t) cost; P1's modes are minima of the reduced cost after eliminating t analytically. For fixed R, t*(R) is the linear least-squares optimum, so the mode sets coincide; the residual is not zero because the nearest-mesh-vertex correspondence is a discretisation (it is the same residual P1 optimises).

The cost has no z>0 constraint, so behind-camera poses are legitimate stationary points of the Theseus objective. Rows with `frac z>0.05 < 0.99` are non-physical and correspond to poses the P1 layer discards.

Random inits are deliberately hard (uniform rotation, t ~ U(-1,1)^3, so most starts are far outside the object's 0.6-1 m depth range). Their success rate measures basin capture from cold start, not detector accuracy.

'GT pose' here means the BOP ground truth; the cost's own global mode is 1.5-8 deg from it on most frames because of the nearest-vertex discretisation, so a GT-init solve cannot be more accurate than that mode.
Solve times exclude objective construction (the 3N-residual objective is built once per frame and the pose variable is reset for each init); they are single-threaded CPU numbers on the login node.
This is an external baseline on P1's *cost*, not a claim about Theseus' performance on published pipelines, and it does not include a posterior.
